paras: The threatened lynching at Graham, North Carolina, was a planned attempt in August 1888 to lynch a prisoner held in the Alamance county jail on a charge of criminal assault on a white woman. Sheriff Hamilton learned of the plan and moved the prisoner to the Chatham county jail at Pittsboro, and no violence against him was reported. Days later the prisoner was reported to have broken out of the Pittsboro jail with another man.

According to the Greensboro Patriot, the prisoner was a Black man, described as "the negro," who had been jailed at Graham "a few days since" for a criminal assault on a white woman. The Charlotte Messenger gave the charge as rape. None of the reports named him or the woman.

Around August 15, Sheriff Hamilton of Alamance county received information that an attempt would be made to lynch the prisoner in the jail at Graham. He removed the man to the Chatham county jail at Pittsboro before any attempt was made. The reports did not describe the would-be lynchers or say how many there were.

On a Friday night shortly after the transfer, two prisoners, Mack Miken and William Minter, broke out of the Pittsboro jail. The Charlotte Messenger said that one of them had been brought from Alamance "a few days before to escape lynching," but did not say which. No report of a recapture or trial was found in the coverage.

The episode appeared only as brief items in columns of North Carolina news. The first, a special telegram to the Richmond Dispatch printed on August 17, gave the sheriff's action in one sentence without the charge or the prisoner's race. The Durham Recorder of August 29 reprinted a Greensboro Patriot brief among its "jottings and clippings" that supplied both, calling the prisoner "the negro." The Charlotte Messenger of September 1 mentioned the threat only to identify one of the escaped prisoners, and none of the papers commented on the planned lynching.

reader.title: Threatened lynching at Graham, North Carolina (1888)
bases: The papers report a plan to lynch a jailed prisoner that was forestalled when the sheriff moved him to another county's jail; no violence is reported (A1, A2, A3).

No one was killed: the prisoner was removed from the Graham jail before the reported attempt (A1, A2), and the threatened mob is never described or counted; the pretext was an accusation of criminal assault on a white woman (A2, A3).

Three reports in different papers agree that Sheriff Hamilton moved a prisoner from Alamance to the Pittsboro jail to prevent a lynching (A1, A2, A3), though A2 is itself a reprint of the Greensboro Patriot.
